v.rationale:
All three implementations work: tests pass (11, 13 and 11), and the probes (bare --days, 0, '007', '+5', ' 5', 99999999, future logins, the exact 90-day boundary) behaved the same in every one. The query scope is effectively identical across all three. So the ranking comes down to output quality, tests and polish.

impl-1 is the most balanced. Its output line is labelled, its tests are idiomatic with frozen time and an exact-boundary case, Pest.php is edited cleanly and Pint passes. Its only real excess is withoutOverlapping(10) on a single server.

impl-2 has the strongest boundary tests, but it logs a bare number, leaves a stray duplicate line in Pest.php, and adds noise: Http::preventStrayRequests, an onOneServer assertion and an unneeded factory state.

impl-3 fails Pint because of import order, prints '1 users', uses a full Validator for one option, has no index, and has weaker tests: no frozen time, no boundary case, and the error assertion only matches the word 'days'.
